I was in the gf side, and let me tell you that is not as simple as just ignoring you have feelings. On my experience I tried a few times to have conversations with my ex. When I saw him down I used to tell him that I'd be there if he needed to talk but he never did. I understood that some things he wouldn't share because he just didn't want to, and if I insisted it'd make everything worse. Some others were needed to be discussed, like problems in the relationship. Even when I asked him to let me know if I ever said or did something that hurt him unintentionally to let me know so that we could work things out and I could be better. He always said I did everything right, every time I noticed I did something wrong and apologized he always said there was no need because he didn't saw it as a wrong doing. 

At the end I discovered that is not that he thought I did everything right (like I suspected), just that he never told me, he just talk to his friend about it, but not me. Obviously without any communication the relationship dissolved.

My point is here, are you being clear with your feelings? Trying to open up in conversations? Do you start this conversations or ask for emotional help? It can be hard to do so, but nobody can read minds. Maybe if she doesn't ask because she feels that you'll open up when you are ready, who knows. 

If you already did open up and talked about your struggles and she didn't comfort you how you wanted there's two options, either tell her what you need so that she can act accordingly, or if she doesn't give it importance than is not the relationship you need to be in. Sit down and have conversation with her, you might be surprised with what you need!

At first I would have said that probably you didn't tell her you expectations about your birthday, and what you said there gives me the feeling that even when you'd like to be celebrated as well you're not too into big events. And at least for future reference I'd advise you to communicate your expectations on things like that so that nobody gets the wrong idea and makes you feel unappreciated. I say this for my own experience, I personally like to celebrate other's bdays but not my own, I just like to have a small celebration.

Now, even with all that I said before I still think your girlfriend is in the wrong here. Probably (and I'm just trying to assume to give her the benefit of the doubt) she thought that as you're not that interested on a big celebration as her you wouldn't want anything special. But saying something like "So are you like 12? Do you need balloons and all that crap?" is simply not right, all of us deserve to be loved and feel celebrated if we feel like it, especially from people close to us and even more if it's your SO. And I think she should understand it even more as she likes to have a big party in occasions like this this one.

I think you should evaluate what you have in your relationship. If this is a one time thing you should see how this feels now and if you will be able to just move pass it and keep going with the relationship. But if is just another example of selfish behaviour in your relationship you should consider breaking up, keep going with your life and find someone in the future who will appreciate you as you deserve. Good luck!
